info.title: Miai evaluation API
info.description:
For measuring a bot's strength against Miai in games you run yourself. Also can be used for live play.

Submit `POST /api/act` with `{"infoset_str": "..."}`. The response is
`{"action": "..."}`: one complete decision from the model serving this site — a
whole combination, `PASS`, a tribute card, or a return card. No room, match id,
other players' cards, or card-by-card prefix loop is needed. Use the **Examples** dropdown in the request body below for a ready-to-send
request at each phase, or copy the complete card-play example here.

### Complete card-play request

```bash
curl https://guandan.miai.moe/api/act/batch \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"queries":[{"player":"PLAYER","input":"Level:J|View:P1|Head:dealt|P1+3c3d3h4d4s5c6s8d8d8s9sTcTsTsJhJsQdQhQsKcKdKhKsAcAdAsRj|FinishOrder:P1,P3,P2,P0|P0:P3:Js|P2:P1:Rj|ReturnFirst:P1|P1:P2:6s|P3:P0:7h|P2-44455:4d4h4s5d5d|P3-55533:5h5s5s3s3s|P0-PASS"}]}'
```

One response observed with the serving weights is
`{"answers":[{"player":"PLAYER","action":"QQQ44:QdQhQs4d4s"}]}`: beat the full house with queens over fours.
Actions are model decisions, not fixed responses promised by the API. This
infoset ends at **P1's turn**, after the following history:

| Segment | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Level:J` | This hand is played at level J: J ranks above A, and `Jh` is wild |
| `View:P1` | The querying player, who must be the player to act |
| `Head:dealt` | Declares that the next segment is the viewer's dealt hand |
| `P1+3c3d…AsRj` | P1's 27 cards as dealt, before tribute and return |
| `FinishOrder:P1,P3,P2,P0` | The previous hand's finishing order, first to last |
| `P0:P3:Js` | Tribute: P0 gives `Js` to P3 |
| `P2:P1:Rj` | Tribute: P2 gives `Rj` to P1 |
| `ReturnFirst:P1` | P1 returns first |
| `P1:P2:6s` | Return: P1 gives `6s` to P2 |
| `P3:P0:7h` | Return: P3 gives `7h` to P0 |
| `P2-44455:4d4h4s5d5d` | P2 leads a full house, fours over fives |
| `P3-55533:5h5s5s3s3s` | P3 beats it with fives over threes |
| `P0-PASS` | P0 passes; now query P1's next action |

`|` separates segments. Seats are the stable tags `P0`–`P3` in turn order
(`P0` → `P1` → `P2` → `P3`); `P0`/`P2` and `P1`/`P3` are partners. They never
rotate between hands: name the actual opening leader and finishers.

### Infoset grammar

A query is the acting player's own record of the hand, in this order:

1. `Level:<rank>` — the level being played, `2`…`A`.
2. `View:P<i>` — the viewer, who must be the player to act.
3. `Head:dealt` — fixed marker for the dealt-hand convention.
4. `P<i>+<cards>` — the viewer's **27 cards as dealt**. Keep this head unchanged
   for the whole hand: tribute, return and plays are replayed from the later
   segments, so never replace it with the current hand.
5. `FinishOrder:P<a>,P<b>,P<c>,P<d>` — the previous hand's finishing order,
   which decides the tribute. The first hand of a match uses
   `FinishOrder:P0,P1,P2,P3` followed by `P0:None`.
6. The exchange:
   - `P<i>:None` — no tribute is paid (first hand or resisted tribute); `P<i>`
     leads.
   - `TributeSelection:<n>` — ends a query while the payers are choosing
     tribute: `n` payers have already chosen (`0` or `1`). Their cards are not
     shown until both choices are revealed together.
   - `P<payer>:P<receiver>:<card>` — a revealed tribute, then `ReturnFirst:P<i>`
     naming the receiver who returns first.
   - `P<receiver>:P<payer>:<card>` — a return, after `ReturnFirst`.
   - `ReturnSelection:1` — ends the second returner's query in a double return:
     the first return card is still hidden from them.
7. Plays in order: `P<i>-<combination>` or `P<i>-PASS`.

Include only what the viewer has seen. Never include other players' dealt
hands, the other payer's undisclosed tribute, or the first return before it is
revealed; a query containing them is rejected. Serialize with nanopokerlib's
`guandan.infoset_str_from_history_str(history)`; the masked string is its own
canonical form, so applying that function to a query must return it unchanged.

### Cards and actions

Cards are two characters: rank `23456789TJQKA` (`T` is ten) and suit `c`, `d`,
`h`, `s`; the jokers are `Bj` (black) and `Rj` (red). Two decks are used, so a
card can appear twice. Hands are sorted by rank `2`…`A`, suits `c`, `d`, `h`, `s`
within a rank, then `Bj`, `Rj`, independent of the level.

The response is exactly one of:

- `TRIBUTE:<card>` while paying tribute, for example `TRIBUTE:Js`.
- `RETURN:P<payer>:<card>` while returning, for example `RETURN:P2:6s`.
- `PASS`, legal only when following another player's combination.
- A combination: a single as the bare card (`Td`, `Rj`); otherwise
  `<shape>:<cards>`, the declared ranks then the physical cards, such as `77:7c7s`
  (pair), `888:8c8h8h` (triple), `55533:5h5s5s3s3s` (full house),
  `23456:6d5c4c3c2s` (straight), `223344:4d4h3c3h2c2s` (three consecutive pairs),
  `333444:4c4c4d3c3s3s` (two consecutive triples), `7777:7c7d7h7s` (bomb of
  four to ten), `45678h:8h7h6h5h4h` (straight flush; the shape names its suit) and
  `BjBjRjRj:BjBjRjRj` (four jokers). Elsewhere a shape names a joker by one
  letter, `B` or `R`: `BB:BjBj` (pair), `555RR:5c5d5sRjRj` (full house). The
  level heart may stand in for another
  card: `3333:3c3d3hJh` uses `Jh` as a three. A lone wild plays as the level
  card itself (`Jh`); older histories may still show one declared as another
  rank, written rank first, as in `A:Jh`.

### Rules and scoring

- 108 cards, 27 per player. Ranks order `2` < … < `A` < level rank < `Bj` <
  `Rj` for singles, pairs, triples and full houses; straights run `A2345` up to
  `TJQKA` by natural rank and never wrap. The two hearts of the level rank are
  wild: each may stand in for any card except a joker.
- The previous hand's last-place player pays its highest card to the first-place
  player: a red joker if held, else a black joker, else a level-rank card (a
  lone wild heart does not oblige this), else the highest other rank; every
  physical card of that rank is a separate choice. If first and second place
  were partners, both losers pay, last place choosing first; the higher tribute
  goes to first place and the lower to second (on equal ranks each payer gives
  to the player seated before them, so `P2` pays `P1`). Holding both red jokers
  between the payers cancels the tribute, and first place leads. Each receiver
  returns one card ranked 9 or lower, never of the level rank. The payer of the
  higher (or only) tribute leads; after equal tributes the player after first
  place leads.
- Players must beat the previous combination with the same shape or with any
  bomb. Bombs rank four < five of a kind < straight flush < six … ten of a kind <
  four jokers. After three passes the last player to play leads again; if that
  player has gone out, the lead passes to their partner.
- The hand ends once both partners of either team are out. The team of the
  first player out wins 3 if the partner finished second, 2 if third, 1 if last;
  the other team loses the same. On this site the winners climb that many levels
  from 2 toward A. A team playing its own A level wins the match by finishing
  first with its partner not last; three failed attempts send it back to 2.

Each query covers one hand. The model sees the level and the previous finishing
order through these segments, so keep them exactly as played.

### Players, batches and limits

Take a player from `POST /api/act/players`: it holds the model's memory of one
seat, game after game, and is yours until it sits idle for five minutes. Then send
`POST /api/act/batch` with one query from each player, 204 at most, and read one
answer for each, in order. A response takes at least 10 seconds however few queries
it holds, so run many players side by side.

A player starts at the start of a game and must play what it was answered: an input
that goes another way ends its game, and the player starts again at the next game.
Sending the same input again returns the same answer.

A malformed body returns HTTP 422. A query that cannot be answered has an `error`
in its answer instead of an `action`. Queries share the model with the games on this
site, one decision at a time, and the games come first, so responses take longer
when the site is busy. The server holds at most 408 queries running or
waiting; a request past that, or for a player when all are taken, receives HTTP 429
with `Retry-After`. Retry with bounded backoff. Players do not outlive a restart of
the server: an unknown player's answer says so, and you take a new one.

`GET /api/act/stats` reports this server process's query traffic since it started:
players held, completed, invalid, failed, rejected and cancelled queries, and each
query's response time, including the wait for the model. `last_24h` adds up the last
24 hours of queries and the addresses they came from, and how many answers were
played as answered (`followed`) or not (`departed`). It resets on restart and
describes no game outcomes; keep complete game records to analyze results.

Every query and its answer is kept, with when it came. The address it came from
is kept for 60 days.
